summary: Registers seven mail transmission type keywords, ESMTPA, ESMTPS, ESMTPSA, LMTP, LMTPA, LMTPS and LMTPSA, for use in the with clause of a Received header. They show whether a message used extended SMTP or LMTP, with encryption or authentication.

eli5.summary: Every email stamps a note about how it traveled. This document adds words for the different travel methods, such as secured ones.

questions: what does esmtpsa mean in received header
subtitle: Seven new keywords that let a Received header record whether mail travelled over ESMTP or LMTP, with encryption or login.

tldr.problem: The Received header in an email has a 'with' clause that names the protocol used for each hop, but no keywords existed to say whether TLS or authentication was used.
tldr.mechanism: This memo registers seven keywords with IANA: ESMTPA, ESMTPS, ESMTPSA, LMTP, LMTPA, LMTPS and LMTPSA. The trailing letters mean authenticated (A), TLS-protected (S), or both (SA).
tldr.outcome: Mail servers get a standard, compact way to leave trace information about each hop, but the keywords are only hints and should not drive filtering or relaying decisions.

today: RFC 3848 is a Draft Standard and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it, so it remains the definition of these keywords.

sections.title: What the Keywords Are For
sections.content:
When a message is passed along, each mail server adds a Received header. Its with clause names the protocol used. IANA keeps a registry of these "WITH protocol types", which held SMTP and ESMTP before this memo.

RFC 3848 adds seven new keywords to that registry. It also asks that the SMTP and ESMTP entries point to RFC 2821, because RFC 821 and RFC 1869 were obsoleted by it.
sections.eli5: Each post office stamps a letter with how it was carried. This document gives the post offices more words to use on the stamp.

sections.title: The Seven Keywords
sections.content:
The three ESMTP keywords are ESMTPA (ESMTP with the SMTP AUTH extension and successful authentication), ESMTPS (ESMTP where STARTTLS was successfully negotiated for strong transport encryption) and ESMTPSA (both STARTTLS and SMTP AUTH).

The four LMTP keywords follow the same pattern: LMTP for plain use of LMTP, then LMTPA, LMTPS and LMTPSA for authentication, STARTTLS, or both.
sections.eli5: An 'S' means the trip was in a sealed envelope and an 'A' means the sender proved who they were. 'SA' means both.

sections.title: Implementation Experience
sections.content: The RFC notes that the ESMTPA, ESMTPS and ESMTPSA keywords had already been implemented in deployed email server software for several years, and that no problems had been reported with their use.
sections.eli5: Some post offices were already using the first three words, and nobody had trouble with them.

sections.title: Trace Information, Not Proof
sections.content:
The keywords give an informal way to track use of high-level security protocols between hops without revealing which mechanism was used. They can help diagnose email abuse after the fact.

They are not normally protected in transport, so an active attacker can modify them, and they do not say which mechanism was used. They should not be used for mail filtering or relaying decisions except in very controlled environments. The RFC also criticises stripping Received headers, which reduces the ability to correct abuse.
sections.eli5: The stamp is a handy clue, but anyone could scribble on it, so do not trust it like a locked door.
